verses.text: “The Kingdom of Heaven is like a landowner who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.
He agreed to pay them a denarius for the day and sent them into his vineyard.
About the third hour, he went out and saw other people standing idle in the marketplace.
He told them, ‘You go work in my vineyard too, and I’ll pay you whatever is fair.’ So they went.
He went out again around the sixth and ninth hours and did the same.
Around the eleventh hour, he went out and found others standing there. He asked, ‘Why have you been standing here idle all day?’
They replied, ‘Because no one hired us.’ He told them, ‘You go work in my vineyard too, and I’ll pay you whatever is fair.’
“When evening came, the vineyard owner told his manager, ‘Call the workers and pay them their wages, starting with the last ones and ending with the first.’
The workers hired at the eleventh hour came and each received a denarius.
When the first workers came, they expected to receive more. But each of them also received a denarius.
They took their pay and grumbled against the landowner.
‘These last workers put in only one hour,’ they said, ‘and you made them equal to us, even though we carried the burden of the day and worked in the scorching heat!’
“He answered one of them, ‘Friend, I’m not treating you unfairly. Didn’t you agree to work for a denarius?
Take your pay and go. I choose to give this last worker the same as I gave you.
Am I not allowed to do what I want with what belongs to me? Or are you jealous because I’m generous?’
“So the last will be first, and the first will be last. Many are called, but few are chosen.”
As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples aside. On the way he told them,
“We’re going up to Jerusalem. The Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and scribes. They’ll condemn him to death
and hand him over to the Gentiles to be mocked, whipped, and crucified. On the third day he’ll be raised.”
Then the mother of Zebedee’s sons came to Jesus with her sons. She knelt before him and asked him for something.
He asked her, “What do you want?” She said, “Promise that my two sons will sit in your Kingdom, one at your right and one at your left.”
Jesus answered, “You don’t know what you’re asking. Can you drink the cup I’m about to drink and be baptized with the baptism I’m about to undergo?” They said, “We can.”
He told them, “You will drink my cup and be baptized with the baptism I undergo. But I can’t grant you seats at my right or left. Those places belong to the people my Father has prepared them for.”
When the other ten heard about it, they were angry with the two brothers.
But Jesus called them over and said, “You know that the rulers of the nations dominate their people, and their officials throw their weight around.
That’s not how it should be among you. Whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant,
and whoever wants to be first among you must be your slave.
That’s how the Son of Man came: not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
As they were leaving Jericho, a large crowd followed Jesus.
Two blind men were sitting beside the road. When they heard Jesus was passing by, they shouted, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!”
The crowd told them to be quiet, but they shouted even louder, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!”
Jesus stopped, called them over, and asked, “What do you want me to do for you?”
They answered, “Lord, we want our eyes to be opened.”
Jesus felt compassion for them and touched their eyes. At once they could see, and they followed him.
